title: Margin-adaptive temperature scaling
question: Can top-two logit margin condition a rank-preserving temperature and improve calibration under Gaussian corruption?
hypothesis: A shrinkage-regularized margin-conditioned temperature lowers paired ECE versus scalar temperature scaling without worse NLL or changed argmax.
treatment: Fit a bounded monotone mapping from clean-calibration top-two margin to a positive per-example temperature, shrunk toward one global temperature.
control: Scalar temperature scaling fit on the identical clean calibration logits and labels.

title: Entropy-binned shrinkage scaling
question: Does entropy-conditioned shrinkage improve post-hoc calibration under corruption?
hypothesis: A small number of entropy bins with temperatures shrunk to a global fit lowers ECE while preserving predictions and NLL.
treatment: Fit bounded temperatures for quantile bins of clean-calibration predictive entropy with global shrinkage.
control: Scalar temperature scaling under the same calibration examples and optimization budget.

title: Logit-norm conditional scaling
question: Can logit norm identify overconfidence modes induced by Gaussian corruption?
hypothesis: A bounded logit-norm-conditioned scalar multiplier improves ECE over global temperature scaling without changing class ranking.
treatment: Fit a regularized affine function of centered logit norm that produces one positive scalar per example.
control: One global scalar temperature fit on identical clean calibration logits.

title: Top-confidence spline temperature
question: Does a low-capacity monotone function of maximum confidence improve shifted calibration?
hypothesis: A three-knot monotone confidence-to-temperature function reduces ECE with no NLL or argmax regression.
treatment: Fit three bounded temperatures over clean-calibration confidence knots and linearly interpolate a positive per-example scale.
control: Scalar temperature scaling fit to the same clean calibration split.

title: Trimmed-loss robust temperature
question: Can robustly fitting temperature reduce sensitivity to mislabeled calibration examples?
hypothesis: Trimming the largest calibration NLL contributions yields lower corrupted-set ECE than ordinary scalar temperature scaling.
treatment: Fit one temperature by deterministic trimmed NLL and bounded search on the identical calibration logits.
control: Ordinary scalar temperature scaling with the same candidate grid.

title: Huberized calibration temperature
question: Does Huberizing example losses improve robustness of temperature fitting?
hypothesis: A Huberized calibration objective improves ECE without degrading NLL on corrupted evaluation data.
treatment: Fit a global positive temperature using a deterministic bounded Huberized loss over clean calibration examples.
control: Standard scalar NLL temperature scaling with the same bounded search grid.

title: Median bootstrap temperature
question: Can aggregation across deterministic calibration bootstraps stabilize temperature scaling?
hypothesis: The median of temperatures fitted on fixed bootstrap subsets reduces ECE variance and mean ECE.
treatment: Fit temperatures on fixed deterministic bootstrap index sets and use their median scalar.
control: One scalar temperature fit once to all calibration examples.

title: Jackknife-averaged temperature
question: Does deterministic jackknife aggregation improve temperature stability under shift?
hypothesis: Averaging leave-block-out temperature estimates lowers paired ECE while retaining NLL.
treatment: Partition calibration data into fixed blocks, fit leave-block-out temperatures, and aggregate their log values.
control: Scalar temperature scaling on the full identical calibration data.

title: Regularized classwise temperatures
question: Can strongly regularized classwise temperatures outperform a global temperature?
hypothesis: Classwise temperatures shrunk toward a global value lower ECE without altering argmax.
treatment: Fit per-class positive scales with strong shrinkage and convert them to a single rank-preserving example scale.
control: Scalar temperature scaling on identical logits and labels.

title: Margin-entropy interaction scaling
question: Is a low-rank interaction between margin and entropy useful for shifted calibration?
hypothesis: A bounded two-feature scale improves ECE beyond scalar temperature scaling without guardrail violations.
treatment: Fit a regularized positive scale from standardized margin, entropy, and one interaction term.
control: Scalar temperature scaling with identical data and seeds.

title: Confidence-tail adaptive scaling
question: Can separately treating only the high-confidence tail improve ECE under corruption?
hypothesis: A tail-specific temperature shrunk to a global temperature improves ECE and NLL.
treatment: Fit one global and one high-confidence-tail temperature with deterministic threshold and shrinkage.
control: A single global temperature on the same calibration split.

title: Low-margin selective rescaling
question: Does rescaling only ambiguous examples improve corrupted calibration?
hypothesis: A bounded low-margin-specific scale lowers ECE without any prediction change.
treatment: Fit a global temperature plus one shrunk scale for a fixed low-margin quantile.
control: Scalar temperature scaling on identical clean calibration logits.

title: Two-resolution confidence binning
question: Do coarse and fine confidence partitions provide complementary calibration signals?
hypothesis: A shrinkage blend of two- and four-bin temperatures improves ECE over a global scalar.
treatment: Fit deterministic two-bin and four-bin temperatures and shrink their log-scale blend to the global fit.
control: Scalar temperature scaling with identical calibration examples.

title: Cross-fit temperature aggregation
question: Can fixed cross-fitting reduce overfitting in post-hoc temperature selection?
hypothesis: Geometric aggregation of fixed-fold temperature estimates reduces held-out ECE.
treatment: Fit temperatures on deterministic folds and geometrically aggregate them without evaluation-label access.
control: Scalar temperature scaling fit once to all clean calibration examples.

title: Target-entropy temperature fitting
question: Can matching a robust calibration entropy target improve corrupted-set calibration?
hypothesis: A bounded temperature matching a trimmed correct-class confidence target lowers ECE.
treatment: Fit one positive temperature to match a robust target derived only from clean calibration logits and labels.
control: NLL-optimal scalar temperature scaling on the same inputs.

title: Calibration-loss ensemble scale
question: Does blending temperatures from NLL and calibration-gap objectives improve robustness?
hypothesis: A fixed shrinkage blend of two independently fitted scalar temperatures lowers ECE without worse NLL.
treatment: Fit bounded scalar temperatures under NLL and a differentiable calibration-gap proxy, then geometrically blend them.
control: NLL-only scalar temperature scaling using the same clean calibration examples.
